chapter: Southern Illinois roadhouse and St. Louis
title: Gang wars, being shot, and meeting Capone
summary: Joe was shot and beaten in the Berger-Shulman gang war while working the roadhouse, and met Al Capone and Purple Gang members there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You said a little while ago on one of the tapes that I didn't pick up on, but I had it in my mind to pick up on it later... You said that you played with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band?

Well, this was a band that... When I left this roadhouse, I almost got killed. That's when I got shot for working in there. That's a story in itself. So in the meantime, I was in the hospital, because I had a bullet crease in my head, and a guy shot me through the knee here, and I got beat up, got mugged by another gang, the Shulman Gang that had started fighting with the Berger Gang. And they put me in the hospital, and I damn near died. In the meantime, Charlie, the head gangster, came there and wanted to know if I still wanted to work for him, and he wanted to

know if... They was going to set these guys up and they was gonna kill some of them, of the Shulman Gang -- which they did. If you read the history of Gangsterism, this was a prominent gang. The Eagle Rats from St. Louis used to come there. I met Al Capone there, I met his brother Ralph, and I met some of the guys from the Purple Gang in Detroit. Because they all used to come there and drink, and I used to talk to them.

One of the Sheldon brothers is the one who really saved my life from getting killed, because the guy had a gun right at my head and was going to kill me. Because one of the guys in the band, the piano player, put out a rumor that we was posin' as musicians, but we was actually a part of the gang and part of Charlie Berger's bodyguards. So these guys laid for us. Like I said, it's a whole chapter almost.

So anyway, after I got in all that trouble, I says, "I'm leaving here." And I told Charlie, I said, "No. If you can, try to get me a Billboard while I'm in the hospital recuperating." He said, "Okay, I'll get you one."
That's the same Billboard Magazine that's still going today.
That's still running today. And that's what they called "the Showman's Bible" at that time. Any time you wanted a job, they had pages and pages for jobs for
musicians, if you wanted to travel. Circuses, minstrel shows, medicine shows, and carnivals -- all of them had live ...(? )...
